name: Bahrain
summary: No personal income tax, no capital gains tax, no tax on dividends or interest, no wealth tax and no inheritance or estate tax. No general corporate tax (46% on oil and gas; 15% DMTT for MNE groups with EUR 750m+ revenue from 2025). VAT 10%. Real estate transfers carry 2% stamp duty (1.7% if paid within two months). About 50 treaties, none with the US.

regimes.name: Bahrain tax residence
regimes.description: No personal taxes on income, gains, wealth or estates.

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax for individuals on any asset.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Real estate transfers bear 2% stamp duty (1.7% if paid within two months), a transaction cost rather than a gains tax.

capital_gains.rate_basis: No PIT regime (PwC); no general taxes on income, sales, capital gains or estates (PwC corporate).
capital_gains.professional_trader: No risk: there is no income tax on individuals or general corporate tax.

dividends.rate_basis: No PIT regime; income not paid in Bahrain is outside local tax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on dividends, interest or royalties.
dividends.treaty_network: About 50 treaties in force (PwC); no treaty with the United States, so US dividends held directly bear 30% US WHT.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No general property tax. A 10% municipality tax applies to rent on property let to expatriates (paid by the owner); this is a rental levy, not a wealth tax.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Succession, not tax, is the issue: personal status (family) law based on Sharia governs inheritance of Muslims, with fixed shares (a son typically takes twice a daughter's share) and at most one third freely disposable by will to non-heirs. How estates of non-Muslim foreigners are handled (home-country law, own religious rules, or Sharia by default) was not verified for this country; non-Muslim families should take local legal advice and hold portfolio assets outside the country or through a structure with a clear governing law.

open_questions: PwC confirms no general tax on estates; a dedicated statement on gift tax was not found (no gift tax is believed to exist).
Treatment of non-Muslim foreigners' estates under Bahraini family law not verified.

residency.tax_residency_test: No personal income tax, so tax residence is not defined for PIT purposes (PwC). Treaty residence certificates are issued by the National Bureau for Revenue (procedure not verified).

routes.name: Golden Residency (property or wealth)
routes.requirements: 10-year renewable residency for property owners and holders of substantial assets; thresholds (commonly reported as BHD 200,000 property) could not be verified because the official NPRA page was unreachable.

routes.name: Employment / investor residence
routes.requirements: Residence permit via an employer or a Bahraini company (100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors; not verified here).

corporate.summary: No general corporate income tax. 46% tax on oil and gas profits. 15% Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax for MNE groups with EUR 750m+ consolidated revenue, financial years from 1 January 2025. No WHT on dividends, interest or royalties. VAT 10%.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed; no Bahrain-US income tax treaty.
